Rashi on Shabbat 107b:10:1.hebrew: הצד נחש - נמי הצידה היא המלאכה, וזה אינו צריך לצידה אלא שלא תשכנו, ואם יודע שתעמוד ולא תזיקנו, לא היה צד:
Rashi on Shabbat 107b:10:1.english: One who traps a snake - [Here] too, trapping is the [prohibited] labor, and this [person] does not need the trapping [itself], only so that it will not bite him; and if he knew that it would stay still and not harm him, he would not trap [it].

Rashi on Shabbat 107b:11:1.english: One who removes a fish - That was already caught while it was still day [before Shabbat].

Rashi on Shabbat 107b:11:2.english: Like a sela - Like the width of a sela.

Rashi on Shabbat 107b:11:3.english: [He is] liable - On account of taking a life, for it will no longer live.

Rashi on Shabbat 107b:11:4.english: Produces mucus - That one touches it and a thread of mucus stretches from the finger.

Rashi on Shabbat 107b:12:1.hebrew: דלדל - עקר, שהפילתו על ידי דלדול זה:
Rashi on Shabbat 107b:12:1.english: Detached - [He] uprooted [it], so that [the animal] miscarried it through this detaching.

Rashi on Shabbat 107b:12:2.english: Bar Hamdurei explained it to me - [That is,] the reason for this matter.

Rashi on Shabbat 107b:12:3.hebrew: כשותא - הומלון, וגדל מתוך ההיזמי מריח הקרקע שההיזמי יונק ממנו:
Rashi on Shabbat 107b:12:3.english: Keshuta - Hops [Old French: homlon], and it grows out of the shrubs from the scent of the ground from which the shrubs draw nourishment.

Rashi on Shabbat 107b:12:4.hebrew: מיחייב - ואף על פי שאינו מחובר לקרקע, כדאמרינן בעלמא (עירובין דף כח:): מאוירא רבי:
Rashi on Shabbat 107b:12:4.english: Is liable - Even though it [the hops] is not attached to the ground, as we say elsewhere (Eruvin 28b): "It grows from the air."

Rashi on Shabbat 107b:1:1.hebrew: למה שמנו חכמים - בשחיטת חולין, אלו שעורותיהן כבשרן. והא ודאי משבשתא היא. אדרבה, למה שמנו חכמים אין להם עור, דהא עורותיהן כבשרן קאמרי:
Rashi on Shabbat 107b:1:1.english: With regard to those that the Sages enumerated - in [Tractate] Sheḥitat Ḥullin, [in the Mishnah,] "These are [the animals] whose skins are like their flesh." And this [baraita] is certainly corrupt. On the contrary, those that the Sages enumerated do not have skin, for they say "their skins are like their flesh."

Rashi on Shabbat 107b:1:2.hebrew: ואמר אביי הכי קאמר אין עור חלוק מבשר - אלא לאותן ד' שלא מנו חכמים: חולד, ועכבר, וצב, ותנשמת. אבל האנקה, הכח, והלטאה, והחומט — אין עורן חלוק מבשרן, ולא הוי חבורה. ומ"מ קשיא לרב:
Rashi on Shabbat 107b:1:2.english: And Abaye said: This is what it is saying, [that] skin is not discrete from flesh - except for those four that the Sages did not enumerate: the weasel, the mouse, the toad, and the mole. But [as for] the hedgehog, the chameleon, the lizard, and the snail — their skin is not discrete from their flesh, and [wounding them] is not [considered] a wound. And in any event, it is a difficulty for Rav.

Rashi on Shabbat 107b:1:3.hebrew: א"ל רבא והא למה שמנו קאמר - ולא טעי תנא בין מנו ללא מנו:
Rashi on Shabbat 107b:1:3.english: Rava said to him: Doesn’t it say, "for what [the Sages] enumerated"? - And a tanna would not err between "enumerated" and "did not enumerate."

Rashi on Shabbat 107b:1:4.hebrew: אין עור מטמא כבשר כו' - והכי קאמרי ליה: דקאמרת לענין שבת יש להן עור, אבל לענין טומאה עורותיהן כבשרן, דאיתרבו מהטמאים — אין עור מטמא כבשר אלא לאותן ארבעה שמנו:
Rashi on Shabbat 107b:1:4.english: No skin transmits impurity like flesh, etc. - And this is what they are saying to him: As for what you say, [that] with respect to Shabbat they have skin, [indeed so,] but with respect to impurity, their skins are like their flesh, for they were included from [the verse] "the impure ones" — no skin transmits impurity like flesh except for those four that they enumerated.

Rashi on Shabbat 107b:1:5.hebrew: מכלל דר' יוחנן כו' - בתמיה, והא קתני התם גבי טומאה דכל ח' שרצים לר' יוחנן בן נורי יש להן עורות:
Rashi on Shabbat 107b:1:5.english: By inference, that Rabbi Yochanan, etc. - [This is asked] as a rhetorical question: isn't it taught there regarding impurity that according to Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri, all eight creeping animals have skins?

Rashi on Shabbat 107b:1:6.hebrew: תריץ הכי - סמי מברייתא "אלא", ותני: אין עור למה שמנו חכמים. ומיהו לרב לא תקשי, דהכי קאמרי ליה: לענין שבת מודינא לך דהחובל בהן חייב, אבל לענין טומאה פליגא, דאין עור לאותן ד' שמנו:
Rashi on Shabbat 107b:1:6.english: Resolve [it] this way - Delete [the word] "only" from the baraita, and teach: "Those that the Sages enumerated do not have skin." However, according to Rav there is no difficulty, for this is what they say to him: "With regard to Shabbat, I agree with you that one who wounds them is liable; however, with regard to impurity, I disagree, for those four [creeping animals] that they enumerated do not have skin."

Rashi on Shabbat 107b:2:1.hebrew: בשרצים שיש להן עורות - לאותן ד' שלא מנו:
Rashi on Shabbat 107b:2:1.english: With regard to creeping animals that have skins - [Referring] to those four that they did not enumerate.

Rashi on Shabbat 107b:2:2.hebrew: נצרר הדם - נאסף ונקשר במקום אחד, שוב אינו חוזר ונבלע:
Rashi on Shabbat 107b:2:2.english: The blood collects - [It] gathers and congeals in one place, [and] it no longer returns and becomes absorbed.

Rashi on Shabbat 107b:3:1.hebrew: מאן ת"ק - דהך מתניתא דאמר בשרצים שיש להן עורות, דמשמע דיש מהן דפטור:
Rashi on Shabbat 107b:3:1.english: Who is the first tanna - Of this baraita, who said [this] regarding creeping animals that have skins, which implies that there are some of them for which [one] is exempt.

Rashi on Shabbat 107b:3:2.hebrew: רבי יהודה היא - דלענין טומאה לא יליף מאלה הטמאים, אלא ההוא דאית ליה גישתא — שעורו עב ויש לו עור ממש — אינו כבשר, ושאינו עב הוי כבשר. והלטאה, משום דעורה עב, משוי ליה כחולדה בהעור והרוטב. הלכך, לענין שבת נמי לאו עור הוא בשלש מהן: אנקה וכח וחומט. אבל לרבנן דהעור והרוטב, שמנו הלטאה בהך שעורותיהן כבשרן, אלמא דטעמייהו לאו משום עור ולאו עור, אלא משום דרשה דקרא; לענין טומאה הוא דפליגי משום קרא, אבל לענין שבת מודו דודאי עור הן:
Rashi on Shabbat 107b:3:2.english: It is Rabbi Yehuda - For with regard to impurity, he does not derive [it] from "these are the impure ones"; rather, that [creeping animal] which has gishta — [meaning] its skin is thick and it has actual skin — is not [considered] like flesh, while [one] whose [skin] is not thick is [considered] like flesh. And [regarding] the lizard, because its skin is thick, he equates it to the weasel in [the chapter] HaOr VeHaRotev. Therefore, with regard to Shabbat as well, it is not [considered] skin for three of them: the anakah, the koach, and the chomet. However, according to the Rabbis of HaOr VeHaRotev, who counted the lizard among those [whose] skins are like their flesh, evidently their reason is not because of [whether it is] skin or not skin, but rather because of a scriptural exposition; it is [only] with regard to impurity that they disagree because of the verse, whereas with regard to Shabbat they concede that they are certainly skin.

Rashi on Shabbat 107b:3:3.hebrew: דברי ר' יוחנן בן נורי - דקתני בההיא ברייתא דלעיל לענין שבת, כיון דלא איפלגו רבנן עליה אלא לענין טומאה, "דברי ר' יוחנן בן נורי ומחלוקתו" מיבעי ליה:
Rashi on Shabbat 107b:3:3.english: The statement of Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri - That which is taught in that baraita above with regard to Shabbat: since the Rabbis disagreed with him only with regard to impurity, it should have [stated], "the statement of Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri and those who disagree with him."

Rashi on Shabbat 107b:4:1.hebrew: מנין לחבורה שאינה חוזרת - ולמילף דההיא דחוזרת לאו חבורה היא, כגון הנך דאין להן עור שנצרר בו הדם — חבורתו חוזרת לקדמותה — או מכה קטנה שלא נצרר הדם:
Rashi on Shabbat 107b:4:1.english: From where [is it derived] that a wound does not reverse - And [this is] to derive that one that reverses is not [considered] a wound, such as those [creatures] that do not have a hide in which the blood collects — [for] its wound returns to its former state — or a minor blow in which the blood did not collect.

Rashi on Shabbat 107b:4:2.english: If you say that it stands [in] spotted marks - And [that] the verse speaks of an actual leopard, which is spotted with [various] colors.

Rashi on Shabbat 107b:4:3.hebrew: אלא ככושי כו' - והאי "נמר" לשון תמורה: "היהפוך כושי עורו ונמר חברבורותיו" — כלומר, וימיר חבורת עורו לחזור לקדמותו, שלא יתקשה העור במקום המכה:
Rashi on Shabbat 107b:4:3.english: Rather, like a Cushite, etc. - And this [word] namer is an expression of exchange: "Can a Cushite change his skin, and [can] his wound be exchanged [venamer chavarburotav]?" — that is to say, [can] he exchange the wound of his skin to return to its original state, so that the skin does not harden at the site of the blow.

Rashi on Shabbat 107b:5:1.english: A camel - Because it is large, he mentioned it.

Rashi on Shabbat 107b:6:1.english: From rams - Reddened rams that were slaughtered for the work of the Tabernacle for their hides.

Rashi on Shabbat 107b:6:2.hebrew: והא אמר מר - בשמעתא קמייתא דמס' ע"ז:
Rashi on Shabbat 107b:6:2.english: And didn't the Master say - In the first passage of Tractate Avodah Zarah:

Rashi on Shabbat 107b:6:3.hebrew: ביצי כינים - קס"ד כינים קטנים כשיוצאים מביציהן:
Rashi on Shabbat 107b:6:3.english: Eggs of lice - [Abaye] initially assumed [that this refers to] small lice when they emerge from their eggs.

Rashi on Shabbat 107b:7:1.hebrew: הטפויין - "שירוץ הטפויין וביצי כינים", מתניתא היא, ולא ידענא היכא תניא:
Rashi on Shabbat 107b:7:1.english: The tippuyin - "The swarming of the tippuyin and lice eggs" is a baraita, and I do not know where it is taught.

Rashi on Shabbat 107b:7:2.hebrew: הצד פרעוש - ממקום שאינו ניצוד ועומד, כגון מעל גבי קרקע או מבגדיו מבחוץ:
Rashi on Shabbat 107b:7:2.english: One who traps a flea - From a place where it is not [already] trapped and confined, such as from upon the ground or from his clothes on the outside.

Rashi on Shabbat 107b:9:1.hebrew: להוציא ממנה לחה - מלאכה שאינה צריכה לגופה היא, שהפתח היא המלאכה, וזה אין צריך להיות כאן פתח מעכשיו:
Rashi on Shabbat 107b:9:1.english: To remove pus from it - It is a labor not needed for its own sake, for the opening is the labor, and this [person] does not need an opening to be here from now on.

Tosafot on Shabbat 107b:11:1.hebrew: כיון שיבש בו כסלע - בניצוד ועומד במים מיירי, מדלא מחייב ליה עד שיבש כסלע:
Tosafot on Shabbat 107b:11:1.english: "When [an area] the size of a sela has dried on it" - [Shmuel] is speaking of [a fish] that is [already] trapped and standing in the water, since he does not hold him liable until [an area] the size of a sela has dried.

Tosafot on Shabbat 107b:1:1.hebrew: אמר אביי אין עור חלוק מבשר כו' - מסקנא דפירכא היא מאביי, דודאי אליבא דאביי פליגי לענין שבת, אבל למאי דמפרש רבא ורב אדא לא פליגי מידי לענין שבת. ותימה הוא: כיון דלא קיימא שינויא דאביי, היכי פריך מינה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 107b:1:1.english: Abaye said: Skin is not discrete from flesh, etc. - This is the conclusion of the refutation [that comes] from Abaye, for certainly according to Abaye they disagree with regard to Shabbat, whereas according to what Rava and Rav Adda explain, they do not disagree at all with regard to Shabbat. And it is astonishing: since Abaye's resolution does not stand, how does [the Gemara] raise a refutation from it?

Tosafot on Shabbat 107b:7:1.hebrew: הצד את הפרעוש כו' ר"י פוטר - משמע דפטור אבל אסור. ואומר ר"י בשם הרב פורת, דאפ"ה אם נושך האדם, מותר ליקחנו ולהשליכו מעליו, דמשום צער שרי; אבל אם הוא באותו ענין על האדם שאינו ירא שינשכנו, כגון על סרבלו מבחוץ, אסור ליטלו, אבל יכול להפילו מעליו:
Tosafot on Shabbat 107b:7:1.english: "One who traps a flea, etc., Rabbi Yehoshua deems him exempt" - This implies that he is exempt [from a sin-offering], yet it is [rabbinically] prohibited. And the Ri says in the name of HaRav Porat that even so, if it is biting the person, it is permitted to take it and throw it off himself, for due to pain it is permitted; however, if it is on the person in such a manner that he is not afraid it will bite him — for example, on the outside of his cloak — it is prohibited to take it [in his hand], though he may knock it off himself.

Tosafot on Shabbat 107b:7:2.hebrew: יש ספרים דגרסי: <abbr title="מאי טעמא">מ"ט</abbr> מחייב רבי אליעזר, לאו משום דפרה ורבה? ושיבוש הוא, דהא אפילו בכינה מחייב רבי אליעזר; ופרעוש נקט לרבותא דרבי יהושע, דאפילו פרעוש פוטר. ושינויא נמי דמשני לא משמע דגריס ליה, <abbr title="ורבינו תם">ור"ת</abbr> נמי מחקו מספרו:
Tosafot on Shabbat 107b:7:2.english: There are texts that read: "What is the reason Rabbi Eliezer deems [one] liable? Is it not because it procreates?" And [this] is an error, for even with a louse Rabbi Eliezer deems [one] liable; and [the baraita] specified a flea to [show] the novelty of Rabbi Yehoshua's [opinion], that even [for] a flea he exempts. Furthermore, the answer that [the Gemara] gives does not imply that it has this reading, and Rabbeinu Tam also erased it from his book:
